_doc: The town's ships (Systems/Fleet.cs), for a town founded on the sea (founding.json kinds with a sea) once its Harbour stands. The harbour's first boat comes with it. Ships: cost gold and timber, crew to man them (fed `ration` food a head a day at sea), a hold for trade runs, a speed (days at sea for each day out the port's region lies), a hull that wears `wear` a day at sea and is patched for `repair` gold a point, `fish` food a day while moored, and `fight` against corsairs. A captain's prowess (1 green to 5 legendary) adds `prowessFish` to the catch and `prowessFight` to every fight, and grows `learn` a voyage. Ports are known settlements not hostile (`minStanding`) along the coast: their region within `reach` degrees of the town's sea, or one of `coastThemes`. Trade runs sell like the airship's (trade.json sky prices, the same gluts) and bring back the port's cheap goods. Corsairs: each run home meets them with `chance` plus `perRing` a ring out (at most `max`), strength `strength` plus `strengthPerRing`; the captain rolls d20 + the ship's fight against 10 + their strength. Lost, they take `loot` of the cargo and `hurt` hull; won, the captain learns and the crew share `prize` gold. Now and then (`raidEvery` days, `raidChance`) corsairs come for the harbour itself: the moored ships and the watch fight them off, or they take `raidGold` gold and `raidFood` food and hole a ship. The stand-in mayor builds the first ships, patches them below `patchBelow` of their hull, and sends a run every `standInEvery` days that clears `standInProfit`.

foes.name: sahuagin raiders out of the reef
a drowned ship crewed by the Choir's dead

voyages._doc: The sea's jobs and passages (Systems/Voyages.cs). A ship's days at sea are its speed times the navigator's roll (d20 + the captain's prowess + the best Survival aboard against 'navigateDc': times navigate[0] on a 20, [1] on a pass, [2] on a miss, [3] on a 1) times the weather (1 + 'weather' times sky.json's 'stormStep' chance for the day's sky over the waters, and the season's wind on the heading up to sky.json's 'wind' either way). Each day out a ship meets something with 'meet' plus 'meetPerRing' a ring out (at most 'meetMax'), one of 'foes' for the ring, fought as sky.json's ship fights. Jobs: 'patrol' the home waters for 'patrolDays' (each patrol turns away 'patrolGuard' of the corsairs' raids), 'scout' a sea land (charted like an airship's scouting), 'strike' a sea site (each gun takes 'strikeShare' of its strength a day in reach, at most 'strikeMost'). A company that sails to an island in the town's own ship (taken before the Sky Dock's lent airship whenever open sea is all that's in the way) brings home 'hold' gold times (ring + 1) of salvage and trade when it wins.

sail: {ship} slips her moorings, {captain} at the helm, bound for {where}.
The harbour bell rings as {ship} stands out to sea for {where}.
storm: A gale catches {ship} off {where}; {captain} runs before it and loses a day.
evaded: {captain} sees {foe} hull-up on the horizon and crowds on sail; they never close.
won: {ship} meets {foe} off {where}. {captain} takes the weather gauge, the guns speak, and {foe} break off.
Off {where}, {foe} come at {ship} and are beaten off with their sails in rags.
boarded: {foe} grapple {ship} off {where}; {marines} meet them at the rail and throw them back into the sea.
repelled: {foe} grapple {ship} off {where} and fight their way aboard before {marines} drive them off. The ship limps on.
lost: {foe} maul {ship} off {where}; {captain} breaks off with the hull stove in.
wrecked: {ship} goes down off {where}, fighting {foe}. Her crew take to the boats.
struck: {ship} is home from {where}: her guns took the fight out of {site} ({share} of their strength).
patrolled: {ship} is home from patrolling the home waters, nothing slipped past her.

guards._doc: Who stands at the rail besides the crew, filling the ship's marine places the heroes leave: 'watch' lends town watchmen (gone from the town's watch while at sea), 'hired' pays sellsword marines 'wage' gold a head a day at sea. 'fight' is what each adds to the boarding.

corsairs.name: the corsairs
win: {captain} sees the corsairs' sails at dawn, runs out the oars and leaves them wallowing; a boarding party that does catch up goes over the side. ({prize} gold of theirs)
lose: Corsairs come out of the sea mist and board {ship}. {captain} saves the crew but not the hold: {lost} {good} gone, and the hull holed.
sunk: {ship} does not come home. A fishing boat finds a spar with her name on it.
repelled: Corsair longboats nose into the harbour by night. The watch and the crews of the moored ships meet them on the quay, and they row off empty.
raided: Corsairs raid the harbour by night: {gold} gold and {food} food carried off, and {ship} holed at her mooring.
